context: a single passage from a letter by John (b) Murray, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: By this day’s post I send you a specimen copy of your book bound— I hope it may receive your approval. Please reply by return & not a moment shall be lost in getting ready the early copies—your instructions seem quite clear & shall be carefully followed. Now as to price—the book from its bulk & size will not be dear at 14/. & this is the price I propose. At this price the edition of 1250 copies will yield about £240—⅔ rds of which will go to the author— The only alternative is 12/.—which will yield no more than £150— In the above statement of probable profits, I have not deducted anything for corrections & omissions— They amount in Clowes’ bill to £72:8:—but I do not wish to deduct any part of them in your case, but to let them go into the general account of expenses Charles Darwin Esq.

I have received your kind note & the copy: I am infinitely pleased & proud at the appearance of my child.— I quite agree to all you propose about price. But you are really too generous about the to me scandalously heavy corrections. Are you not acting unfairly towards yourself? Would it not be better to at least share the £72’s 80? I shall be fully satisfied; for I had no business to send, though quite unintentionally & unexpectedly, such badly composed M.S. to the printers. I will pay for my copies, whenever you like. I am so glad that you were so good as to undertake the publication of my Book.— My dear Sir | Yours very sincerely | Charles Darwin P.S. | Please do not forget to let me hear about 2 days before the copies are distributed.
